before.name: Steven Charles Hamilton
before.description: Steven Charles Hamilton was a Free Speech Movement and antiwar organizer who helped organize Stop the Draft Week and became one of the Oakland Seven. An eleven-week conspiracy trial ended with all seven acquitted in March 1969. Hamilton had separately been convicted with four activists for trespass during a protest against Navy recruiting at the University of California, Berkeley, and of contempt for holding a press conference about that case. Contemporary reports place him in jail in June and July 1969 while serving a 75-day term arising from those demonstration misdemeanors.

before.name: Terry Cannon
before.description: Terry Cannon was a Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee organizer, founder of The Movement newspaper, and one of the Oakland Seven prosecuted for organizing the October 1967 Stop the Draft Week demonstrations. The Seven were acquitted in March 1969. In a separate prosecution arising from profanity used during a demonstration, Judge Elton C. Lawless sentenced Cannon to three months in county jail on November 22, 1968. Cannon served two weeks before his lawyer obtained his release on appeal bail.
